paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Before a single bad thing happens to Job, the Bible tells us who he is: "blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil" (Job 1:1). Then the LORD Himself says there is "no one on earth like him" (Job 1:8). So when the hard stuff hits, nobody can say Job had it coming.

Now look at Satan's question: "Does Job fear God for nothing?" (Job 1:9). He's saying Job only loves God because God blesses him, and he says Job will "surely curse You to Your face" if it all goes (Job 1:11). Then everything goes, one messenger after another, and Job stands up, tears his robe and falls to the ground and worships. He says, "The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD" (Job 1:21). I think that's the whole point, baker: he worships with empty hands.

So here's what it means for you. A good life with God doesn't mean a life with no loss, and losing things doesn't mean God has walked off. Faith that only shows up when the oven is warm and the cookies are coming out perfect isn't the faith Job shows us. And notice how the chapter ends: "In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing" (Job 1:22). I'm telling you, this story isn't over, and there's a lot more to Job.
